# Acquire a syndrome-conditioned receiver without normalizing rare branches

28 October2026. Author derivation, source-informed numerical oracle and explicit counterexample. Independent review requested. This is channel-adapted recovery using ordinary qubit instruments and SDPs, not a new optimization algorithm or a claimed advantage over equally informed standard methods.

## Instrument and correct objective

Let E_s be the actual trace-decreasing qubit-input to qubit-output channel conditioned on terminal syndrome s, BEFORE the final syndrome-conditioned correction. Its Pauli transfer matrix is

    M_s = [[a_s,b_s^T],[c_s,T_s]].

The sum over s is TP; individual branches generally are not. A deterministic CPTP qubit receiver D_s has transfer matrix [[1,0],[t_s,R_s]]. The complete instrument-and-receiver channel has entanglement fidelity

    F_e = (1/4) sum_s [a_s + b_s dot t_s + Tr(R_s T_s)].

This follows from F_e(Lambda)=Tr(M_Lambda)/4 and matrix multiplication. Importantly b_s describes input-dependent syndrome probability. Its dot product with receiver translation is absent from the TP single-channel quasi-inversion objective, but present here. Applying a TP Procrustes/unitalization theorem separately to normalized syndrome branches is invalid in general: the conditioning is input dependent and not a linear TP channel.

Use unnormalized recovery Choi J_s on output tensor input, J_s>=0, Tr_output J_s=I. Define

    C_s = (1/8) sum_(i,j=0)^3 (M_s)_(j,i) sigma_i tensor sigma_j^T.

Then the branch objective is Tr(C_s J_s), including terms which vanish under the TP constraint. The exact optimum separates into S four-by-four SDPs. The dual is minimize Tr(Y_s) subject to I tensor Y_s>=C_s. All syndrome branches count, without postselection. Per-branch unitary optimization is the proper SO(3) Procrustes solution for T_s, with a_s added as the constant term; it is generally a lower bound on full CPTP recovery.

## Strict nonunital example and a useful failure on the actual pipeline

Consider two branches E_0(rho)=<0|rho|0>I/2 and E_1(rho)=<1|rho|1>I/2. Every conditional unitary leaves the mixed output unchanged, giving total F_e=1/4. Resetting the output to |s> using the syndrome gives F_e=1/2, which is optimal since this channel is entanglement breaking. # The fixed-record quantity is also distance to the closest constant record

28 October2026. New author addendum to the frozen GOVERNING_BRANCH_RECOVERY_v1.md (SHA256 d09353188b8c2171be328d024b10da3a84826c185e2a7e209626386e7d5a6084). Independent review pending. No preceding numerical result changes.

The frozen source proves ||M_record−K_a||_diamond=L=sum_s||b_s|| for K_a(rho)=Tr(rho)sum_s a_s|s><s|. It conservatively does not assert optimization over constant records. The following short argument establishes that stronger statement without changing the original source.

For an arbitrary probability distribution q, let K_q(rho)=Tr(rho)sum_s q_s|s><s|. Apply M_record−K_q to one half of a normalized Bell state. Its syndrome-s reference block is

    [(a_s−q_s)I+b_s dot sigma]^T/2.

The block eigenvalues are[(a_s−q_s) plus/minus ||b_s||]/2, and its trace norm is

    max(|a_s−q_s|, ||b_s||).

Therefore ||M_record−K_q||_diamond is at least the sum of these maxima, which is at least L for every q. Since q=a attains L by the original theorem,

    min_(constant classical-record channels K) ||M_record−K||_diamond = L.

This proves K_a is a minimizer, not necessarily the unique one. Constants are channels with the SAME classical record alphabet; no larger quantum output or record postprocessing is silently admitted. Combining with the fixed-POVM attainment in the frozen source gives

    max_(instruments E with record POVM F) [F_e(best CPTP receiver)−F_e(best unitary receiver)]
      = (1/4) min_(constant classical-record channels K) ||M_record−K||_diamond.

The maximum is attained by E_s(rho)=Tr(F_s rho)I/2, using reset-to-b_s receivers. The interpretation is an extremal relation between actual qubit record leakage and receiver choice, not an assertion of nonunital advantage for every instrument or of coherent preservation by the attaining erased-output instrument.

# Higher-dimensional boundary: zero record leakage does not force unitary recovery

28 October2026. Author exact counterexample using the standard Werner–Holevo channel. Independent review pending. This is a scope boundary for the new qubit theorem, not a new Werner–Holevo construction or a claimed quantum-storage capability.

For odd dimension d>=3 define the CPTP unital channel

    N(rho) = [Tr(rho) I − rho^T]/(d−1).

A Kraus representation is K_ij=(|i><j|−|j><i|)/sqrt(d−1), one for each i<j. Their adjoint products sum to I. Treat N as an instrument with ONE classical outcome. Its record is exactly constant, so its record-channel distance to constants is zero.

Nevertheless a nonunitary recovery can outperform every unitary recovery. Choose recovery D=N. Direct composition gives

    N²(rho) = [(d−2)Tr(rho) I + rho]/(d−1)²,
    F_e(N²) = 2/[d(d−1)].

For a unitary recovery U, the Kraus trace formula gives

    F_e(U composed with N)
      = [d − Tr(U conjugate(U))]/[d²(d−1)].

The trace is real. The unitary W=U conjugate(U) has conjugate-paired spectrum because conjugate(W)=U† W U, and det(W)=1. For odd d, its unpaired real eigenvalues include at least one +1: the number of −1 eigenvalues is even by the determinant, while the total number of real eigenvalues is odd. Thus Tr(W)>=2−d. Equality is attained by real orthogonal U having one1×1 block +1 and(d−1)/2 blocks [[0,1],[−1,0]]. Consequently

    max_unitary U F_e(U composed with N) = 2/d².

At d=3, the actual CPTP candidate D=N achieves1/3 while all unitary receivers achieve at most2/9. Hence no universal higher-dimensional version of the qubit zero-leakage receiver conclusion is possible. We do NOT need or assert that D=N is the full-CPTP optimizer. The lower bound from this explicit candidate already gives a strict separation.

Crucially D=N is UNITAL. The failure is that unital channels in dimension3 and above need not be mixtures of unitaries, unlike qubits. Therefore the relevant higher-dimensional comparison is **nonunitary versus unitary** recovery, not necessarily nonunital versus unitary. The qubit theorem remains a statement in which any premium requires a nonunital receiver because every unital qubit receiver is mixed-unitary.
